_comment: Loose daypart guardrails, in server-local time (TZ set on the dj container). `hours` is a [start, end) range in 24h clock; a window that wraps past midnight (like night, or the weekend techno slot) is written as start > end and handled that way in code -- the early-morning tail is attributed to the day whose evening started it. `days` is optional: a list of weekdays (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday, i.e. Python's datetime.weekday()) the entry applies to; omit it (or leave unset) for every day. Entries are matched top to bottom, first match wins -- so more specific day/hour overrides belong above the generic fallback dayparts. `mood` weights are matched against the same six-dimension mood vector AudioMuse-AI stores per track (happy/sad/aggressive/party/relaxed/danceable) - values are relative targets, not required to sum to 1, and are only used when `artists`/`genres` don't already supply a pool (or as the fallback when that pool comes up empty). `artists` and `genres` pull straight from Jellyfin instead of the mood catalogue -- for a themed hour that wants specific acts or a specific tag rather than just a vibe. `exploration` (low/medium/high, default medium) loosens how far from the mood target the adaptive picker is willing to wander -- higher means more variety, lower means it sticks closer to the target. Only used for mood-based picks, not artists/genres.
